body: Split-adjusted ₹12.4 (Mar 2009) → ₹3,292 (Aug 2024) ≈266x; ₹2,327 on 19 Nov 2026 (−29%). Twin engine: trailing P/E ~2.2 at the Mar 2009 trough (TTM EPS ₹5.7) → 48.6, about 22x rerating × implied EPS ~12x. About 55% of the log-return was the multiple, the highest share among the long-duration cases here. Drawdowns: −89% (2006–09, before), −34% (2013), −32% (2014–16), −48% (2018–19), −39% (2024–26). Early signal: a niche global off-highway (agri, OTR) replacement-tyre exporter (~85–90% exports, Europe the largest market) priced like a commodity truck-tyre maker; P/E 6–13 through 2010–2015 while EPS compounded; Bhuj greenfield plant (first tyre 2012, completed ~2015) roughly doubling capacity to ~300k t. Investors who saw 'global niche, Indian cost base' held a 9-year rerating to 24–36x by 2017–2021. Stalled: EPS flat FY22–26 (~₹74), ROCE down from ~24% to ~11% after heavy capex (carbon black, Bhuj expansions), weak European agri demand and freight. Lesson: the biggest rerating wins come from a market's mis-classification (commodity → niche franchise); when returns on capital fall, the rerating stops.

data.early_signals: niche global OHT exporter at P/E 2-6; capacity doubling at Bhuj
data.lesson: mis-classification rerating; watch ROCE after big capex
data.note: Prices: screener.in weekly closes, split/bonus-adjusted. P/E = trailing (TTM) from screener chart; 'implied EPS x' = price multiple / P/E multiple.

title: Balkrishna Industries 2009–2024: off-highway tyre niche, rerating from P/E 2
